title: Serotypes, tropism, and promoters
objective: Explain how AAV serotype sets which cells get infected, and what a promoter adds on top.

steps.title: Serotype = the virus's outer shell
steps.body: [[AAV]] comes in different **serotypes** (AAV1, 2, 5, 8, 9, PHP.eB, retro…). The [[serotype]] is the capsid — the protein coat — and it determines **[[tropism]]**: which cells the virus enters efficiently, and whether it spreads or stays local. Picking a serotype is picking which cells (and route) you'll hit.

steps.title: Promoter = a second layer of control
steps.body: Inside the virus, a **promoter** drives the payload. A broad promoter (CAG, hSyn for neurons) expresses in many cells the virus enters; a cell-type-specific promoter narrows it further. So specificity can come from **serotype (entry) + promoter (expression) + [[Cre]]-dependence (the switch)** — stacked together.

steps.prompt: Match each component to the specificity it provides.
pairs: Which cells the virus enters / its route
Which entered cells actually express the payload
steps.explanation: Real experiments stack these: route + entry + expression + genetic switch + location.

steps.scenario: You inject an AAV and get strong expression — but in the wrong cell types near your target.
steps.prompt: Which change is most likely to fix the cell-type specificity?
options: Switch to a serotype/promoter with better tropism for your target, and/or make the payload Cre-dependent in a cell-type Cre line
steps.explanation: Off-target expression is a tropism/promoter/switch problem. More virus makes it worse. Narrow entry (serotype), expression (promoter), or add a Cre-dependent switch.
steps.followUp: Titer and volume affect how MUCH and how FAR, not which cell types.

sources.citation: Tervo DGR, et al. A Designer AAV Variant Permits Efficient Retrograde Access to Projection Neurons. Neuron 92:372-382 (2016).
sources.note: Shows how a capsid variant changes tropism/route (retrograde). DOI confirmed via Crossref.

reviewNotes: Tropism vs. promoter vs. switch is the key mental model; leads into retrograde.
